source: How... who ransacked my personal belongings?
Someone must know. About me. About my brother.
Lord Polonius collapsed during our game. He's not breathing.
I shouldn't be here. They'll find me.
I shouldn't be here. He'll find me.
Lady Ophelia. Surely you've seen her?
Guildenstern. She slipped away at some point, and I cannot find her.
Please, will you watch for me? If you see her, tell me.
It's-- it's extraordinarily unusual for her to not tell me where she's gone.
The last time it happened... was when Hamlet spurned her, years ago. I almost lost her then.
But this must be something else. Something she never told me. I'm afraid.
I-- I don't mean to trouble you. I apologize. I'll take my leave of you now.
What brings you down here, my lord?
Something delicate.
I have a favor to ask of you.
And what are you asking me to take care of now?
I'm ordering you to keep it private.
It's something my wife cannot know about. Not yet. Not now. I'll tell her, but in my own time.
I fear with the state she's in, this letter would only send her reeling into the abyss.
You've threatened me in the past. What makes you believe I have any obligation to be discreet?
Because of the love you bear for my wife, I should hope.
This would be the end of her. Think on that, and keep this among your belongings.
Do your men have a particular habit of snooping in your things?
They each understand the kind of severe and unrelenting punishment I would levy on them.
It's safe here, for now.
Wah hah hah! That's the Bernardo I know.
Good. It's settled, then. I'll return to you in time, when I'm ready to show her what's written inside.
Father. I've come to take you from this place.
Unlock the door.
What's happening? Who's there? I can hardly see.
Allow me to help you out, Lord Polonius.
Has the King determined my fate?
Claudius? Truly? Then why are you here?
I did not believe the King's order to imprison you was done in good faith, or out of a genuine need for security.
It appeared he did this simply to punish you. In light of his passing, I would like to restore you to a place of dignity.
Of course, I will still expect your compliance in all matters of state. But for now, you are free.
Thank you. Thank you all.
Laertes, please have the servants bring food and water. I have felt such a chill these last few days. All my strength has left me.
God's wounds, I thought I would die in there.
Suspected I might find you here.
I heard a little something from Ophelia, and had the thought to seek you out.
A 'little something?' Very discriminating of you to reveal your source!
I want to ask about you and Hamlet. I rather suspect you won't want to be asked, which only makes the asking more worthwhile.
Your assessment is correct.
I understand some of this may be painful for you now that Hamlet's gone.
But I also know-- or suspect-- that you are not someone who collapses under his grief.
Correct again.
As I recall, you remained close to his side for quite a long time, didn't you?
After all, when Guildenstern and I met you, Hamlet had already been at school for a year. And your presence in his life predated that.
When did you first begin following him around?
You make me sound like a little lap dog.
Aren't you?
I began following Hamlet after the last war with Norway came to its conclusion, when Hamlet's father drove his blade through Fortinbras the Elder's heart.
I was a soldier then, but never fancied myself a career military man.
Too much work. Not enough job security. And a poor use of my excellent taste in food, wine, and art.
King Hamlet, seeing that I was something of a learned man, made a request of me.
Hamlet was to be educated at Wittenberg soon. But Hamlet's father was worried about him.
Of course, you remember what Hamlet was like before his father's death.
He was wild in a different sort of way then. I remember him diving nude into the Elbe river in midwinter.
And then he called out to us to join him...
Which of course we were never going to do. What was he thinking?
None of us ever really knew. And now it's too late to find out.
That's really Hamlet in a nut shell. One never knows what he's thinking.
So King Hamlet sent you along to Wittenberg to watch over Hamlet. Is that it?
Yes. That's it.
Unlike other trusted men in the King's employ, Hamlet and I were not so dissimilar in age that it would appear strange for me to accompany him.
And Hamlet was well aware of my role. He and I disliked one another immensely at first. I found him far too bold a flavor for my tastes, and he found my very presence stifling.
But over time, we developed a healthy respect for one another. That respect became trust, and that trust became friendship.
Just friendship?
What are you implying?
I want to leave no room for misinterpretation. After all, in many places, your mere insinuations could have me executed.
Horatio, you ought to know me better than that. How many of my lady loves did you meet at Wittenberg?
That's why I'm here. I knew I needed to speak with you if no one else would.
So that's what this is about.
Fine. If you must hear it, let me say it, then. I came to love Hamlet.
I've never said it to anyone else, least of all to him.
And now I never shall.
And he spent all these years not knowing?
Well, I wouldn't say that. Just that I've never said the words.
There was... one evening. The both of us were staggeringly drunk. And the night got away from us, so to speak.
I thought--
I thought to myself the next morning: If he cares for you as you do him, he'll say something.
But he never did.
And so, neither did I. And the silence just sort of stretched all these years.
You've been carrying the weight of something like this all alone. It must have been heavy.
Have you ever thought of sharing it with him?
I-- I have. But I am afraid, in my heart of hearts.
His life is full of so much darkness right now. He's in the worst place I've ever seen him. How can I contribute to that?
Horatio, I'm no expert when it comes to matters of social finesse, as you've no doubt witnessed. But there's one thing I know for certain.
You cannot shoulder this burden forever, waiting for a 'right moment' which may never arrive.
You've got to be earnest with Hamlet. What is it they say? Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
I have been afraid of this too long, and for what reason?
I never thought myself a man who avoided the difficult conversations.
So you'll speak with him?
If my lady suggests it.
Then who am I to refuse?
Thank you, Rosencrantz.
Any time. Any time at all. I hope the conversation runs to its due course.
I-- I have. But something happened to him recently. I don't know that he even sees me when he looks at me, right now.
His mind's fully gone.
Then-- don't carry this alone. Let me carry it with you.
Guilda and I are going to depart Elsinore soon. Circumstances being what they are, it simply feels like the right time to move on.
Won't you come with us?
I-- I suppose I could. This place holds no meaning to me anymore without him.
Where will you go?
We've no idea. We never do. Perhaps we'll go somewhere a little warmer to shake the chill that's descended here.
That's all I needed to hear.
Consider me intrigued. But give me time to think upon it.
I think it took saying all this out loud to understand for myself what I needed to do.
You have my thanks for being the echo I needed.
Any time.
Let me carry it with you.
Guilda and I are going to depart Elsinore soon, now that Hamlet's gone.
Mind an interruption?
From you? Never.
I see. Excellent. I have something to-- ah-- to discuss with you.
What's wrong? You're trembling.
Has some new horror taken place?
No. No, it's nothing like that.
I wanted to ask you about the past. There's something that's been on my mind for quite a while now.
Do you remember that night in Wittenberg, during that first year?
Perhaps. It all feels so distant now. What night do you mean?
I think you know precisely what I mean. And I don't think either of us can hide from it anymore.
Horatio, you're talking nonsense. I don't remember that night.
Let's go inside, shall we?
Wait. Don't run from this. Please.
This is all so serious! Must it be so serious? Why? Why can't we leave what happened in the past?
Because I need to understand.
I think you know what I'm about to say.
I've been in love with you for a long time, Hamlet.
Haven't you got anything to say in response?
I... I don't know. This is sudden.
Let's say that I did remember what happened that evening.
Have I ever given you any indication of inappropriate feelings since then?
Hamlet, what would be inappropriate about feelings like that?
I don't know, exactly. But I know that whatever happened between us, I have put it to rest in the echoes of the past.
And I don't think I ever had the capacity to feel whatever it is you're feeling now.
Then that's the answer to my question. We needn't belabor the point further.
I know what it's like to love someone who doesn't care for you.
I know how painful that is. And if that's how you've been feeling all this time, then it must be agonizing.
I am far too old to agonize over unrequited love. Lingering disappointment, on the other hand, is not beyond me.
Of course this isn't the answer I wanted to hear. But it's the answer I have.
I do love you in a way. But it isn't like that, and it never will be.
Maybe... if I weren't who I am... if I weren't a Prince of Denmark... maybe things would be different.
But what I am is solid, by circumstance of my birth. I can be no other man. And it means that some pieces of me must remain locked away forever.
I will always be your most ardent and faithful friend. But when it comes to matters of love, that's different.
You deserve someone who isn't me, Horatio.
So that's it, then. That's how this ends.
Somehow I thought it'd be more than that. I played that conversation in my head a thousand times.
And in the end, I had my answer in just a scant few minutes.
I've a new wound to nurse.
But still, I sense that this wound will heal faster.
